# Exercises {#sec-m3-exercicios}

```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(Matrix)
library(readxl)

colunas <- c("ano", "perfil", "sh2",
             "pais_origem", "uf_origem", "cidade_origem", "instalacao_origem",
             "pais_destino", "uf_destino", "cidade_destino", "instalacao_destino",
             "tku")

cabotagem <- readxl::read_excel("dados/cabotagem_tku_2025.xlsx", na = c("", "-"))
names(cabotagem) <- colunas
cabotagem <- cabotagem |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.character), str_squish)) |>
  dplyr::filter(tku > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(uf_origem = stringr::str_to_upper(uf_origem),
         uf_destino = stringr::str_to_upper(uf_destino))
```

## 1. SQL instead of `dplyr`

Answer with **one SQL query in DuckDB**, on the coastal shipping CSV: what is the total TKU by
cargo profile, only for destinations in the Northeast?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```{r}
library(DBI); library(duckdb)

con <- duckdb::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT \"Perfil da Carga\" AS perfil,
         COUNT(*) AS ligacoes,
         SUM(\"TKU (t x km)\") / 1e9 AS tku_bi
  FROM read_csv_auto('dados/cabotagem_tku_2025.csv')
  WHERE \"UF de Destino\" IN ('AL','BA','CE','MA','PB','PE','PI','RN','SE')
  GROUP BY perfil
  ORDER BY tku_bi DESC
")

duckdb::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

Column names with spaces need double quotes in SQL. It is one more argument for
standardising names on input, as we did in module 1.
:::

## 2. Sparse matrix

Build the interstate coastal shipping OD matrix as a `sparseMatrix`, with states in the rows and
columns. What is the density of the matrix (fraction of pairs with flow)?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```{r}
od_uf <- cabotagem |>
  dplyr::filter(uf_origem %in% state.abb | TRUE) |>     # keeps all of them, including the EEZ
  dplyr::summarise(tku = sum(tku), .by = c(uf_origem, uf_destino))

zonas <- sort(unique(c(od_uf$uf_origem, od_uf$uf_destino)))

m <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
  i = match(od_uf$uf_origem, zonas),
  j = match(od_uf$uf_destino, zonas),
  x = od_uf$tku / 1e9,
  dims = c(length(zonas), length(zonas)),
  dimnames = list(zonas, zonas)
)

c(zonas = length(zonas),
  pares_com_fluxo = length(m@x),
  densidade = round(length(m@x) / length(zonas)^2, 3))

round(m[1:6, 1:6], 2)
```
:::

## 3. Production, attraction and balance

From the matrix in exercise 2, build the table of TKU produced, attracted and the balance by state, and
make a diverging bar chart of the balance.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```{r}
#| label: fig-ex-saldo
#| fig-cap: "TKU balance (attracted − produced) by state"
margens <- data.frame(
  uf      = rownames(m),
  emitido = Matrix::rowSums(m),
  atraido = Matrix::colSums(m)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(saldo = atraido - emitido) |>
  dplyr::arrange(saldo)

ggplot(margens, aes(x = saldo, y = reorder(uf, saldo), fill = saldo > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1a5b8a", `FALSE` = "#b3402a"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Balance (billion t·km)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```
:::

## 4. Concentration of the corridors

How many state pairs concentrate 80% of the TKU? Compare with the result of module 1, which was
computed by pair of municipalities. Why do the numbers differ?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```{r}
od_uf |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(tku)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(part_acum = cumsum(tku) / sum(tku)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pares_totais = dplyr::n(),
    pares_ate_80 = sum(part_acum < 0.80) + 1
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(proporcao = round(pares_ate_80 / pares_totais, 3))
```

Aggregating by state concentrates more than aggregating by municipality: several different municipal links
add up in the same pair of states. Every concentration measure depends on the unit
of aggregation. That is why it must be stated together with the number.
:::

## 5. Maximum grade

In the slope case study (@sec-m3-declividade), how many kilometres of each
alternative exceed an 8% grade? And what is the 95th-percentile grade?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

```{r}
#| eval: false
segmentos |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    km_acima_8 = sum(comp_m[abs(rampa_pct) > 8], na.rm = TRUE) / 1000,
    p95_rampa  = quantile(abs(rampa_pct), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = alternativa
  )
```
:::
